fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-results.agency: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections
fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-results.title: Election Results Reporting System: August 18, 2026 Primary Election, Data Download Utility (official results extract): state offices
fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-results.note: The same file the federal loader keeps (OfficialResults=Y), one row per county, party, contest and candidate; the Governor and Cabinet, Senate, House and circuit judge contests are read. Votes are the county rows summed, checked against the Division's Summary Reports (fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-summary-cab-rep, fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-summary-cab-dem, fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-summary-leg-rep, fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-summary-leg-dem, fl-dos-2026-sl-primary-summary-jud-nop); every candidate's county sum equals the statewide Total there and every precinct reported. The results carry no write-in line (write-in candidates are not on a Florida primary ballot), so shares are of the candidates' votes. The names stored are the candidate list's. A field is a party primary with two candidates or more; 19 circuit judge contests decided on August 18 are not stored.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 the Secretary of State's notices of the general election list 156 county commission and county council seats in 66 of Florida's 67 counties, 210 school board seats, 96 county judgeships and 1,961 seats on the boards of 814 special districts (community development, fire, soil and water conservation and others), and in a few counties a charter review board, clerk of the circuit court, county attorney, county mayor, supervisor of elections or tax collector. School board members and county judges are nonpartisan and are voted on first at the August 18 primary election; a seat is on the November ballot only when no one won a majority then, or when a write-in candidate has qualified. Sheriffs, property appraisers, tax collectors, clerks, school superintendents and supervisors of elections are otherwise elected in presidential years, next in 2028, and cities, towns and villages vote on days their own charters set.
local_calendar.s: Florida Division of Elections, Notices of General Election for 2026 (one for each county); Florida Statutes, sections 100.041, 98.015 and 105.051

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Florida Division of Elections' candidate list for local offices as read on October 1, 2026, which the Division offers as an unofficial reference (it sends readers to the county supervisors of elections for county candidates): 2,075 candidates in 2,437 contests for county commissions, school boards, county judgeships, a few other county offices and special districts. The contests are those the Secretary of State's notices of the general election name, and each candidate is placed in a county and district by finding the same name, office and seat on that county supervisor's own page. In 1,164 contests the candidate is unopposed and in 157 the August 18 election settled the seat, so no name is printed in November; 352 contests have a name on the ballot. Not loaded: city, town and village offices; 89 candidates whose county could not be found; the 510 candidates the list marks as defeated, withdrawn, not qualified or deceased; ballot questions; the printed ballot order; and local primaries.
local_coverage.s: Florida Division of Elections, Candidate Tracking System (candidate list, Local Candidates, 2026 Election); the Secretary of State's Notices of General Election; the candidate pages of the 67 county supervisors of elections

gaps.p: Florida
gaps.r: Florida's cities, towns and villages take their own candidates' filings and vote on days their charters set; the Division of Elections' list has no city offices, and no one official list covers them. Some county supervisors' pages do show city candidates (171 headings for offices on neither the notices nor the Division's list were seen and left out, nearly all of them city offices), but not which are on the November 3 ballot.

gaps.p: Florida
gaps.w: the order of names on the printed ballot
gaps.r: Neither the Division's list nor a county supervisor's candidate page states the order in which names are printed; each county's sample ballot does, and those are not read here yet.

gaps.p: Florida
gaps.w: candidates whose county the Division's list does not give
gaps.r: The Division's list gives each candidate's office and seat but not the county or the district, so a candidate is placed only when the same name, office and seat is on a county supervisor's own page. 89 candidates still on the ballot or elected unopposed could not be placed that way (Fire Protection Districts 31, Soil & Water Conservation Districts 30, Community Development District 15, Special Tax Districts 4, Board of County Commissioners 3, Mosquito Control Districts 2, Water Control Districts 2, Hospital Authority 1, Port Authority 1) and are left out; the seats they filed for show here without a candidate.
